summary: Defines a Telnet option that lets a client tell the server where the user is located. It is a small extension to Telnet.

eli5.summary: When you phone a help desk they may ask where you are calling from. This option lets a remote login tell the other computer where the person is.

questions: how does telnet send user location
what is the telnet send-location option
subtitle: A Telnet option that lets a user's Telnet program tell the server where the user is physically located.

tldr.problem: Logged-in user listings show names and locations, but for network users the location is often no more than the originating site name.
tldr.mechanism: The SEND-LOCATION option (code 23) lets the user Telnet offer the location with IAC WILL SEND-LOCATION and later send it in a subnegotiation of ASCII printable characters.
tldr.outcome: The server can display the user's real location in addition to the site name, if its system can make use of the information.

today: RFC 779 is a Proposed Standard, and the metadata records no RFC obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: Why Send a Location
sections.content:
Many sites list users currently logged in with names and locations (see the NAME/FINGER protocol, RFC 742). The location helps physically find a user who is nearby or call them, since a nearby phone number is often included. For network users the location is often no more than the originating site name.

This option lets the user's Telnet program send the location to the server Telnet for display in addition to the site name. The same function is already in the SUPDUP protocol (RFC 734).
sections.eli5: A list of who is online is more useful if it says which room they are in, not just which building.

sections.title: Commands
sections.content:
The option is SEND-LOCATION with code 23. IAC WILL SEND-LOCATION requests or agrees to send the user's location. IAC DO SEND-LOCATION requests or agrees to have the other side send it. The WON'T and DON'T forms refuse or demand the other side not use the option. The default is WON'T and DON'T.

The location itself travels as IAC SB SEND-LOCATION <location> IAC SE, where the location is a sequence of ASCII printable characters terminated by the IAC SE.
sections.eli5: One side offers, the other accepts, and then the location is sent as a short line of normal letters.

sections.title: How It Is Used
sections.content: When the user Telnet knows the user's location, it should offer to send it by sending IAC WILL SEND-LOCATION. If the server's system can make use of the information, as the ITS sites can, the server replies IAC DO SEND-LOCATION. The user Telnet is then free to send the location in a subnegotiation at any time.
sections.eli5: Your computer asks 'want to know where I am?'. If the answer is yes, it can tell the location any time.
